newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Hun Sen says Taiwan office to be closed.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen says Taiwan office to be closed.

text.p: Cambodian co-premier Hun Sen said on Tuesday Phnom Penh authorities would close Taiwan's representative office in Cambodia in response to alleged Taiwanese involvement in supporting forces loyal to ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Hun Sen, who ousted Ranariddh on July 6, said Taiwanese investors were not involved in the affair and they should continue business as usual.
"Phnom Penh authorities have decided to close the representative office for Taiwan," Hun Sen told a meeting of foreign investors.
Earlier, Hun Sen said unidentified Taiwanese people, including one armed forces general, had supported Ranariddh's forces before fighting erupted between troops loyal to the two premiers on July 5.
"It is not revenge, but just a measure to find out who is involved in this incident," he said. "A general came to Phnom Penh through this office." He did not elaborate.
"The Taiwanese companies here were not involved at all, and they are advised to carry on as normal," he said.
